Resolution: fleet/node_modules is NOT on factory/'s upward resolution path (factory/ and fleet/ are siblings, no root node_modules), so the module loads the SDK and zod with a top-level-await loader that tries the bare specifier first, then ../fleet/node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/sdk.mjs (the path the task's Context names), then a createRequire anchored at fleet/package.json. One static-looking import in effect, robust to whichever layout Task 1's install leaves.

Per-clause: note -> kata.comment(projectId, task.uid, body) once, answers the uid the answer carried; hand -> one patchMetadata with {'work.attention':'needs-human','work.attention_msg':reason}; settled -> candidate membership checked here, patch value is a JSON STRING of {symbol,file,task:task.id} (metadata is flat+dotted, CONTRACT.md metadata-dotted-flat), a non-candidate makes NO kata call and answers 'not among' + every candidate; sibling_fact -> one kata.getIssue(uid), the text block is bare JSON of the issue's metadata so a reader can JSON.parse it, and a rejection answers 'no fact: ...' rather than rejecting.

Reading of leg (a). The Proof offers two routes to the four tool names — 'the instance's registered tool list, or the config's tool handlers exported for the exam'. I take the first: factoryTools' answer is the real createSdkMcpServer config, and its .instance carries the registered tool table. Measured against @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.275 in a scratch install: createSdkMcpServer({name,version,tools}) answers {type:'sdk', name, instance}, and instance._registeredTools is an object keyed by tool name whose entries carry a function .handler (older MCP server versions spell that .callback). So the exam reads the table off the instance and invokes entry.handler(args, {}) for legs (b)-(d). It does NOT invent a second export on factory/tools.mjs — Produces names only factoryTools, and an exam that accepted an invented export would grade a shape the contract never defined. To stay version-proof rather than pinned to one private field, the accessor tries _registeredTools/_tools/registeredTools and then any own property of the instance that is a non-empty object of handler-bearing entries; whichever it finds, the assertion is on the tool NAMES, not on the accessor.

The exam imports nothing but node builtins and ../../../../factory/tools.mjs — no zod, no MCP client, no network — so its only red at BASE is the absent module.

Why the fake's shapes are what they are: kata.comment answers the mutation projection (flat {uid, revision, short_id, ...}) exactly as fleet/kata-client.mjs projects it, so 'the comment's uid' is read off a flat .uid; kata.getIssue answers the ISSUE projection carrying .metadata, dotted-flat per CONTRACT's metadata-dotted-flat row. patchMetadata's real arity is (projectId, uid, patch, revision) but M2/M3 spell three, so the exam asserts the first three and says nothing about a revision argument.

One place the exam is tighter than the leg and looser than nothing: M3 spells the whole patch as { 'interface.settled': <JSON string> }, so the exam equals the patch's key set to exactly ['interface.settled'] and requires the value to be a string that JSON-parses to {symbol,file,task}.
